title: Distinct Points Reachable After Substring Removal
summary: Given a string s consisting of moves 'U', 'D', 'L', and 'R', representing moves on an infinite 2D Cartesian grid, and a positive integer k , you must remove exactly one contiguous substring of length k from s .
statement: Given a string s consisting of moves 'U', 'D', 'L', and 'R', representing moves on an infinite 2D Cartesian grid, and a positive integer k , you must remove exactly one contiguous substring of length k from s . Starting from the coordinate (0, 0), follow the remaining moves in order. Return the number of distinct final coordinates that can be reached.
constraints: s has one to 100,000 moves drawn from U, D, L, and R.
Remove exactly one contiguous substring of length k.
Count distinct final coordinates over every possible removal.
hints: The endpoint after removal equals the full-walk endpoint minus the removed window displacement.
Store prefix x/y coordinates so every window displacement is available in constant time.
For each window end, subtract prefix[end]-prefix[end-k] from the total and add the resulting coordinate to a set.
This formula is exactly the displacement of all retained moves, and the set removes duplicate endpoints.
editorial: This formula is exactly the displacement of all retained moves, and the set removes duplicate endpoints.

tests.explanation: The three removals end at (-1,1), (-2,0), and (-1,1), giving two distinct points.
Removing the entire walk leaves the origin as the only endpoint.
